title: Project plugin controls — decisions before the full UI

steps.headline: How should the new switches first appear in projects you already have?
steps.today: Skills and bundled plugins already work in existing projects. You decided these controls must not silently disable anything that works today; new marketplace downloads will instead start inactive everywhere.
steps.problem: The proposed defaults for ordinary projects do not necessarily match what an older project can already use. Applying them retroactively could turn a working skill off.
steps.proposal: Choose the starting view for existing projects. In both options, a choice you make afterward takes precedence and new marketplace downloads start off.

options.label: Show what works today
pros: Existing projects keep their working skills, and the switches honestly show which are available.
cons: An older project may initially have more switches on than a brand-new project.

options.label: Show inherited state
pros: Distinguishes older behavior from choices you made with the new controls.
cons: Adds a third state to understand and makes it harder to see what the assistant can use.

steps.path: Projects → skills and tools on a second device
steps.headline: Should syncing personal skill files be required in the first build?
steps.today: A skill inside a synced project folder can travel with that project's files. A skill in your personal folder sits outside those projects, so project sync does not carry it. You said you would like personal skills to travel too.
steps.problem: A project choice may arrive on a second device before the personal skill file does. The choice alone cannot make that skill run there.
steps.proposal: Choose whether to build a separate personal-skill sync path now or show the missing skill and add that sync path as a later piece of work. Neither option silently installs marketplace plugins.

options.label: Sync personal files now
pros: Your personally added skills work across your devices without copying files.
cons: Needs a separate, safe sync design before this feature can be built.

options.label: Show missing for now
pros: Project controls can be built first; you can see the saved choice and which device lacks the file.
cons: You must add the personal skill on that device until personal-file sync is built.

steps.path: Projects → skills and tools on a second device
steps.headline: What should a project show when an outside item is missing on this device?
steps.today: Your project choices should sync, but files installed from elsewhere do not auto-install. Marketplace plugins can offer Install; an outside skill, plugin or server might not have a one-click installer.
steps.problem: Hiding the entry makes a saved choice look lost. An Install button would promise a download YouCoded may not know how to perform.
steps.proposal: Choose how to show an outside item until it exists locally. A missing server still needs local setup and never syncs its credentials.

options.label: Show with local setup
pros: Keeps the project choice visible and explains that the file or server must be added on this device.
cons: There is no universal one-click fix for externally installed items.

options.label: Hide until present
pros: The page only lists what this device can use.
cons: A synced project setting can seem to vanish and reappear across devices.

steps.headline: Should Claude Code opt-in be part of the first build?
steps.today: These new project switches are planned for YouCoded's own assistant first. Claude Code currently has its own settings; you decided YouCoded must not change them without an explicit explanation and consent.
steps.problem: Showing a switch as if it controls Claude Code before the consent flow exists would be misleading. Adding that flow now would also widen this first build.
steps.proposal: Choose the first-build boundary. In either option, Claude Code settings are never silently changed.

options.label: YouCoded assistant first
pros: The controls can be built and tested without changing Claude Code settings; the UI can state their scope.
cons: Claude Code conversations will not follow these project switches yet.

options.label: Include Claude Code opt-in
pros: One build can cover both kinds of conversation.
cons: Requires a separate consent design and testing against Claude Code's own configuration before this feature is ready.
